In the Vietnamese form a long bamboo stick rests at both ends on forked branches driven into the ground, a cord is tied to the middle of the stick and runs to a thin board covering a hole in the ground. In the African form, the guio môkoun, a horizontal cord is stretched and the vertical cord is not tied at the middle, so the horizontal cord divides into a long and a short segment; a short stick strikes the long segment for a low note and the short one for a high note. A beginner first fixes the position of the stick or the cords, then practises striking the long and short segments.
